_authority: This file was WRITTEN by the graphql lane on 2026-10-09 because it did not exist: the board read `no spec`, which is not the same as zero gaps, and nothing could tell a reader what this lane admits to. Every number below is either (a) measured by `validation/m14/fixtures/graphql/census-graphql-grammar.mts` — a production-path walk of the whole admitted corpus, its full output committed beside this file — or (b) attributable to a named programme run. NOTHING here is a classification by the F8 census (`script/m12/bash-node-types-compare.ts`'s counterpart for this lane has not been run): the `handled_verified` / `internal_silent` split below rests on a LITERAL SCAN of the analyzer's PascalCase comparisons plus the observed node-type vocabulary, which is a weaker instrument than the census and is labelled as such on both buckets. Where this file does not know something it says `UNMEASURED`.

_measured.corpus: gql-gqlgen — 143 tracked .graphql/.gql files, all parsed, 0 failures
_measured.firing_instrument: bun script/m14/firing-check.mjs GRAPHQL — 6 types fired, 120/120 parsed (even stride)

handled_verified._description: Node types the analyzer CONSULTS at a type position (a PascalCase literal compared against the node's kind, extracted by literal scan) AND that the pinned grammar produces on this corpus. A type here means the analyzer DECIDES on it, not that its behaviour is pinned by a fixture — this lane has NO committed fixtures yet, which is itself a gap entry (GQ-G5). Types the analyzer consults but that this corpus does not exercise are listed separately below rather than counted as verified.
handled_verified.consulted_but_not_observed_note: Five literals the analyzer compares against that the 143-file corpus never produced. `SourceFile`/`GraphQL`/`Query` are the vendored grammar's alternate root and entry names (the corpus's root is `source_file`, snake_case, plus `Document`), and `InlineFragment`/`Extension` are shapes the corpus does not contain — an inline fragment and a bare extension node. UNMEASURED: whether these are dead branches (the F8 class) or shapes another corpus would exercise; the F8 census is the instrument that decides it and has not been run for this lane.

internal_silent._description: Node types the pinned grammar PRODUCES on this corpus that the analyzer's literal scan never consults. This bucket is a WORKING LIST, not a ruling: the programme's standard is that a type here is structural plumbing (punctuation, comments, wrappers) and correctly emits nothing, and that a type which is NOT plumbing is a gap. Each entry below is marked by what it looks like, and NONE has been verified by a fixture yet — GQ-G4 tracks that verification.
internal_silent.extension_kinds_note: The analyzer handles extensions through an `EXTENSION_TO_DEFINITION` map and a `type.endsWith("Extension")` test, so these kinds ARE reached — the literal scan above cannot see a dispatch that is not a literal comparison. UNMEASURED: the map is the authority and has not been read against these seven names; recorded here so the next turn checks it rather than re-deriving it.
internal_silent.value_and_selection_note: Literal values inside arguments/`DefaultValue`. `ERROR` is the universal tree-sitter recovery node (every parser produces it; the wasm ABI's node-type table does not list it) and one file in this corpus has one. UNMEASURED whether any of these should produce a relationship; they are listed so the question is asked.

gap._description: Confirmed or suspected unemitted semantics, as a MACHINE-READABLE ARRAY because a prose-only gap field is what produced a wrong '57 gaps' count in this programme. The board counts this array. FOUR entries are the four silent relationship types the firing instrument reports; each is `severity: UNMEASURED` because this lane has not yet counted the construct on the corpus — the honest state is 'nobody has measured the denominator', and the next turn replaces it with sites/files or an implementation. GQ-G5 records that the lane has no fixtures at all, which is why nothing in this file can be called pinned.

gaps.missing: The analyzer emits no `calls` edge. Whether GraphQL HAS a call-shaped construct is the question the denominator must answer, and three candidate shapes exist that must each be counted or refuted on the tree: a field SELECTION (`user { name }` — the closest thing to an invocation), a directive APPLICATION (`@deprecated`), and an executable OPERATION entry point (`query Foo`).
gaps.next_step: Count each candidate shape on the 143-file corpus and the whole `.graphql` corpus, then either emit (a field selection as `calls` would duplicate the `references` edge already emitted — that duplication is the thing to measure before implementing) or rule with the count.
gaps.provenance: firing instrument 2026-10-09: `calls` SILENT, and the whole-corpus census emits 0.

gaps.missing: GraphQL HAS inheritance-like constructs the analyzer models differently: `extend type X` (a type EXTENSION, which the analyzer folds into the extended type as members with `metadata.inExtension`), interface IMPLEMENTATION (emitted as `implements`), and union membership (emitted as `uses`). Whether any of them is an `extends` edge in the ontology's sense — a type declaring another type as its supertype — is unmeasured.
gaps.next_step: Count `TypeExtension`/`TypeSystemExtension` nodes (69 files / 88 nodes and 68 files / 83 nodes observed) and decide whether an extension is an `extends` edge or, as the analyzer currently assumes, membership folded into the type.

gaps.missing: CORRECTED: `imports` is NOT absent from the language. The firing instrument reads 0 because the gql-gqlgen corpus contains no import form, but on the GATE's wider population (1,606 tracked .graphql files in 22 repos) the analyzer emits 6 `imports` edges, all of them .graphql paths (`c.graphql`, `b.graphql`, `./10.model.graphql`), and all 6 are unresolved at sample scope. So the construct exists and is EMITTED; the silent reading is a corpus artefact, and the remaining question is only whether those 6 paths should resolve (are the target files in the same project?).
gaps.next_step: Check whether each of the 6 import targets names a file inside its own project; if yes the edge is an in-corpus import the gate can resolve, if no it is a path-addressed module outside the run's key space.

gaps.missing: GraphQL declares types; it does not construct instances. No constructor syntax exists in the grammar.
gaps.next_step: Confirm against the grammar's own node-type table (no constructor node type) and the corpus (0 candidate nodes), then rule INAPPLICABLE with both counts rather than prose.

design_decision.description: What this analyzer has DECIDED, as the file itself states it. These are quoted from the analyzer's own header contract and marked UNVERIFIED-BY-ME: the next turns confirm each against the tree before any of them is called a ruling of this spec.

decisions.question: What is an `extend type X` — a second symbol, or members of the extended type?
decisions.resolution: The analyzer's header states: an extension's members are emitted with `ownerName` = the extended type and `metadata.inExtension = true`; whether the extension also produces a symbol depends on whether the same file DECLARES the type (a pre-pass decides), because a second symbol would be a duplicate identity while a file with only the extension needs one for the `contains` edge to have a source.

decisions.question: How is a field selection targeted, given that an executable document does not carry the parent type?
decisions.resolution: The analyzer's header states: a selection is qualified `<Type>.<field>` only when the document itself says what type the selection is on (a fragment or inline fragment type condition); otherwise the target is the bare field name and `metadata.selectionPath` carries the full path. This is the one decision that directly shapes the 455 ambiguous column, because a bare field name is declared once per type that has it.

decisions.question: Does `implements` flatten the left-recursive `ImplementsInterfaces` tree?
decisions.resolution: The analyzer's header states: `ImplementsInterfaces` is left-recursive, so `A & B & C` nests as `I > I > I`, and every `NamedType` in the subtree is collected — correct for the nested and the flattened shape alike. The census observes 113 `implements` edges in 21 files, so the shape occurs and is measurable.

label_coverage._description: UNMEASURED. This key exists because the fleet's spec shape has it and a missing key reads as a claim of nothing to declare. Each of the six firing types needs an explicit label contract (what its source and target ARE) before it can be counted as covered; the next turns measure them per type rather than assert them here.

_incoming_side._description: The second acceptance criterion, MEASURED this time rather than quoted. `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts graphql graphql 60` reproduces the programme run exactly: `FAIL - 455 ambiguous + 2,317 unresolved of 11,158 edges` (capture: validation/m14/fixtures/graphql/incoming-graphql-60.json), and the lane's census (`validation/m14/fixtures/graphql/probe-graphql-incoming-split.mts`, which imports the gate's own rule) AGREES with it edge for edge: 8386 resolved / 455 ambiguous / 2,317 unresolved. No edge carries an external marker today.

split_at_sample_scope._how: The 2,317 unresolved, classified by EVIDENCE rather than by convenience. `--repo-wide` (the whole-project key space) is NOT yet in this measurement: load on the shared laptop was 15-19 during the run and the project key space parses every file of every sampled repository. The split below is therefore the SAMPLE-scope split, and the IN-CORPUS column is UNMEASURED rather than empty, because a declaration outside the 60 parsed files is invisible to this scope by construction.

external_licensed_by_the_specification.language_fact: The GraphQL specification predeclares the five built-in scalars, its introspection types and its executable/type-system directives; no project file declares them and the spec forbids redefining the built-in scalars. That is the evidence a marker is allowed to rest on, and the arbiter refutes the claim if a project declares the name itself.
external_licensed_by_the_specification.marker_state: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED (next item). `isExternal` must be the BOOLEAN `true` — a string is inert and two lanes lost 88 and 185 edges to exactly that.

in_corpus.why: A target declared by a file outside the 60-file stride is indistinguishable from an absent one here. The bash lane's equivalent measurement moved 266 of 845 edges into this column once the project key space was built; the same run is the next item for this lane.

uses: a type name no file in the project.reading: Most of these are FIELDS of introspection types reached without their owner (`name`, `kind`, `ofType`, `description`, `args` are all `__Type`/`__Field` fields) — a class the lane can either qualify at emission or rule, and the count is the price of each.

uses: a directive with no definition in.reading: Federation and custom directives whose definitions live in a schema this project does not carry. Not spec built-ins, so no language fact licenses them as external.

ambiguity_characterised.finding: The ambiguity is fully explained by key non-uniqueness, measured rather than assumed: 421 published keys are declared more than once in their project and **exactly 455 edges target a non-unique key** — the two numbers are the same column. Top names from the gate's worklist: `Error.message` 26, `Error` 19, `Query` 17, `PageInfo` 12, `schema.query` 9, `@key` 8.
ambiguity_characterised.ruling_candidate: Irreducible by emission alone: `Query` and `Error` are declared in several schema files of a project, and a bare `Query` target genuinely does not name one. The lever, if one is taken, is target QUALIFICATION (`Type.field`), which the analyzer already does where the document names the type; the 455 names are the ones where it does not.

key_uniqueness.note: Recorded because this programme's `#`-suffixed keys made nine lanes' claims unverifiable before the separator moved, and the supervisor asked this lane to check before trusting any name-based count. This lane publishes ZERO keys containing `#` — the separator worry does not apply here — and the duplicate-key count is the ambiguity column above.

_incoming_side.next_step: Run the same census with `--repo-wide` when load allows, to move edges from `unresolved` into the sample-budget column and to give the IN-CORPUS column a real number; then implement the boolean `isExternal` marker on the three spec-builtin classes (2,188 edges) and re-run the gate at both scopes.
